specification.objective: Make profile-local IPC readiness explicit and ensure both unload and failed-start cleanup drain in-flight LLM handlers before releasing context; preserve plugin-only scope, private paths, and protocol validation.

requirements.statement: When no same-process Agent context is available, the Dashboard AI client connects to a Magi-owned Unix-domain socket scoped to the active Hermes profile and invokes only complete_structured through the Agent's existing ctx.llm.

The profile-root OS lock is acquired before any IPC directory creation/chmod, alias, or socket mutation and held across complete start/stop; unload and failed-start cleanup stop accepting work and drain in-flight ctx.llm calls without a fixed deadline before releasing the context.

Fallback TMPDIR path components are inspected before canonicalization; user-owned symlink components and unsafe/foreign-owned directories are rejected, trusted root-owned system symlinks are accepted only when their resolved target chain is safe; checked private runtime/profile directories constrain alias and lock operations; the profile-root lock is a private regular single-link file.

The protocol accepts only bounded structured-completion inputs, recursively bounds schema depth/nodes/bytes, validates response shapes, rejects unsupported methods, and never logs prompts, memory content, credentials, or raw provider errors.
The bridge remains local and profile-path scoped; same-OS-user local processes are explicitly documented as within the trust boundary because Hermes profiles are not OS isolation boundaries.
Existing same-process behavior, explicit AI consent, memory safeguards, and Hermes configuration remain unchanged; only Magi plugin code, its README, and IPC regression tests change.

A duplicate startup adopts an existing listener only after a bounded fixed protocol probe confirms it is a compatible Magi IPC endpoint; the probe invokes no LLM operation and unknown methods remain rejected.
Regression fixtures use unique private short temporary roots and controlled listeners so Unix socket path length or setup races cannot mask the behavior under test.

The listener-ready signal is set immediately when the serving thread enters serve_forever, independent of service_actions polling; failed startup shuts down and joins the serving thread before closing the listener and draining handler threads.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A Dashboard API subprocess uses the profile-local bridge to call fake Agent ctx.llm and receives parsed/text/provider/model output; on the clean baseline, the integration test fails with the existing unavailable-context message.

A fresh long-profile path creates its own hashed alias without pre-created directories; unsafe TMPDIR ancestry and user-owned TMPDIR symlinks are rejected; trusted macOS system symlinks resolve to safe targets; socket permissions are verified.

Concurrent and duplicate starts serialize to exactly one live owner; a non-owner stop preserves the listener; owner unload removes the endpoint; unload remains pending until an in-flight structured LLM request finishes.
Unknown methods, malformed/nested/oversized schemas, invalid request/response shapes, and provider exceptions fail safely; raw provider details do not reach the client or logs.
Existing explicit AI route tests, repository verification, documentation, and unchanged Hermes source/configuration pass the required checks.

Concurrent starts serialize before directory setup; normal unload and failed-start cleanup remain blocked past client timeout while ctx.llm executes, then finish after it returns; documentation states both drains may wait indefinitely.

A hard-linked profile-root lock is rejected before plugin-data directories are created; an active socket is adopted only after a valid bounded Magi probe; incompatible listeners are neither adopted nor removed.
Host-side socket paths in regression fixtures stay within AF_UNIX limits, and an actively accepting incompatible endpoint is deterministically distinguished from a Magi listener.
The profile-root lock is held through startup and cleanup, including directory setup, stale inode recovery, endpoint binding, and unload.
Readiness is signaled independently of service_actions; a deterministic failed-start test proves listener cleanup waits for an in-flight provider call and leaves no socket or serving thread.

invariants.statement: No Hermes source, Hermes configuration, profile isolation setting, credentials, or memory data is modified by bridge setup or tests.
Memory is sent through ctx.llm only when the user explicitly invokes an existing AI action; the IPC bridge never applies an AI proposal to memory.
The endpoint uses Unix-domain sockets only, the active profile path, restrictive filesystem permissions, inode-aware locking/cleanup, and listener-owner-aware lifecycle.
No prompt, memory content, credential, or provider exception detail is written to logs or returned as a transport error.
Processes running under the same OS user are trusted; the bridge does not claim to isolate mutually untrusted same-user processes or Hermes profiles.
After plugin unload completes, no IPC request handler is executing against ctx.llm; unload has no fixed deadline and may remain pending until a provider returns.
A client adopts only a protocol-compatible Magi listener; the health probe is bounded, fixed-response, and never invokes ctx.llm.
A failed listener startup cannot leave a serving thread or socket behind, and cleanup does not release ctx.llm while a handler still uses it.

forbidden_states.statement: AI calls fail solely because Dashboard and Agent do not share a Python process or module registry.
The IPC endpoint is network-exposed, shared across profile paths, removed by a non-owner, left active after owner unload, or accepts arbitrary LLM methods.
Untrusted/symlinked fallback directories, malformed/oversized nested values, hard-linked lock files, raw provider exceptions, Hermes source/configuration, or memory stores are exposed or modified.
Concurrent start/stop races unlink another live listener, unload releases ctx.llm during an active handler, or an incompatible socket is adopted as Magi.
Unload is described as time-bounded when no provider-call cancellation guarantee exists, or the health probe invokes an LLM operation.
A startup failure bypasses the in-flight drain, or listener readiness depends on a polling callback that may not execute before timeout.

inputs.statement: User reports that /magi stats succeeds while Review memory with AI and Compact with AI continue to fail; user authorized a local profile-restricted bridge in the Magi plugin that stops on unload.
Existing runtime_bridge.py stores ctx only in process memory; dashboard/plugin_api.py raises when its process has no matching Agent context.
Independent review identified untrusted long-path TMPDIR handling, listener ownership/cleanup, stale socket races, insufficient nested bounds, and absent response-shape checks.
Final independent review requires explicit concurrent-start and blocked-handler unload coverage.

Independent review found TMPDIR symlink canonicalization, hard-link/lock path integrity, ambiguous indefinite unload, and missing protocol identity verification; fresh long-profile startup was independently reproduced as working without a pre-created hash alias.

The initial v4 regression fixtures used long pytest temp paths and an uncoordinated listener; they were corrected to use short private roots and a controlled response, with expected failures reproduced on the v3 implementation.

Independent review identified that the prior endpoint lock was acquired after directory setup; the lock is moved to the existing profile root and now protects the entire lifecycle, with a hardlink regression test.

Independent review found failed-start close/join ordering and service_actions-based readiness; the revised contract requires explicit thread-entry readiness and drain-before-release on failed startup.

outputs.statement: A tested profile-local IPC bridge between Dashboard API and Agent ctx.llm, secured for the documented same-user trust boundary, lifecycle-bound to the owning plugin registration/unload, with concise privacy documentation.

failure_semantics.statement: If the profile socket is unavailable, untrusted, malformed, or oversized, the request fails safely without credential access, memory mutation, or prompt/provider detail disclosure; existing Agent commands remain usable.
